Evelyn Zhou: Hello everyone! Evelyn here 12 joining ML Infrastructure remotely from Toronto. Excited to be here. Quick setup issues: I cant access the private model repo (403), and my CUDA toolkit install errors out on driver mismatch. Who should I ping? Also, any tips for onboarding to the eval infra? :wave:
Jorge (IT): welcome Evelyn :tada: For repo access, can you paste the exact git clone error? For drivers, what's your GPU model and mac/os/linux?
Evelyn Zhou: thanks Jorge. Clone error: `fatal: unable to access 'https://git.redwood.internal/ml-models.git/': the requested URL returned error: 403` I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 on a ThinkPad with an RTX A2000. Driver install failed with `nvidia-smi: command not found` after running the apt package.
Priya (ML Eng): hey Evelyn, I'm the eval infra owner this sprint. We'll add you to the repo once IT confirms SSO group. Eval infra lives in `git://infra/evals` and we use conda envs + containerized runners. I'll DM a quick walkthrough and some starter prompts.
Jorge (IT): Evelyn, added a ticket to elevate your SSO groups. Meanwhile try `git config --global credential.helper cache` and ensure your Okta session is active. For the GPU, run `sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall` then reboot. If `nvidia-smi` still missing, send me `dmesg` and `lsmod | grep nvidia`.
Evelyn Zhou: ok running `ubuntu-drivers autoinstall` now. Also I noticed the onboarding doc mentions developer VPN for cloning internal repos. Do I need it for `git.redwood.internal`?
Hana (People Ops): welcome! You should have VPN access, yes. If you don't, ping Jorge after the drivers. Also FYI onboarding lunches are Fridays at 12 PT if you want to join remotely. :ramen:
BuildBot: Onboard checklist: Evelyn Zhou added to group 'ml-infra'. Tasks: 1/5 complete. https://redwood.internal/onboard/2112223334
Evelyn Zhou: driver install succeeded after reboot, `nvidia-smi` shows the A2000. Thanks Jorge! Trying git clone again...
Priya (ML Eng): once you have repo access, clone `git.redwood.internal/ml-models` and run `scripts/bootstrap.sh` to pull submodules and create the conda env. If you hit conflicts, ping me or open a PR to the onboarding branch.
Jorge (IT): I've confirmed your Okta groups were updated. You should be able to `git clone` now. Also gave you access to `vpn-remote` group.
Evelyn Zhou: clone worked 12 pulled and ran `scripts/bootstrap.sh` but conda env fails on pytorch build: `RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime`. Any advice?
Priya (ML Eng): likely a mismatch between CUDA toolkit in the env and driver version. Check `nvcc --version` and the CUDA version pinned in `environment.yml`. We usually pin to CUDA 11.8 for A2000. You can try `conda install pytorch torchvision torchaudio cudatoolkit=11.8 -c pytorch -c nvidia` inside the env.
Evelyn Zhou: `nvcc --version` shows 11.7. I'll try upgrading the toolkit. Thanks! Also really appreciate the warm welcome — happy to jump on a pairing session this week to go through the eval pipelines.
Hana (People Ops): love to hear that. Welcome again Evelyn! We'll add you to the "New Hires - April" lunch invite. :tada:
Evelyn Zhou: pairing sounds great, Priya. I'll grab a 30m slot on your calendar tomorrow. And thanks everyone for the quick help 12 I can access the repo and runners now.
